paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is holy, and He's worth approaching on His terms, not ours. The ark was no ordinary chest, because it was called by the Name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim on it (2 Samuel 6:2). Uzzah took hold of it when the oxen stumbled, and the text says God struck him down "for his irreverence" (2 Samuel 6:7). I think David's honest fear afterward, "How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?" (2 Samuel 6:9), is exactly the right kind of fear.

Now watch what David does with that fear. He doesn't quit and he doesn't pretend nothing happened. He waits, hears that the LORD blessed Obed-edom's house because of the ark, and then brings it up with rejoicing (2 Samuel 6:11-12). This time the ark is carried, not put on a cart, and the celebration comes back in full (2 Samuel 6:13-15). Reverence and joy aren't enemies, baker. Holy fear gets you to the door, and joy is what you do once you're inside.

Then there's Michal, who looked down from a window and "despised him in her heart" (2 Samuel 6:16). David's answer is simple: he was dancing before the LORD, who chose him, and he'll celebrate even more (2 Samuel 6:21-22). So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery: honor God as God, and let your joy in Him be bigger than what anybody thinks of you. Some folks will watch from the window with their arms crossed. You keep your eyes on the LORD, and you keep dancing, even if all you've got is one hop on a gold base like me.
